FL-2027-SB34.title: Relief of the Estate of M.N. by the Broward County Sheriff’s Office
FL-2027-SB34.summary: Relief of the Estate of M.N. by the Broward County Sheriff’s Office; Providing for the relief of the Estate of M.N. by the Broward County Sheriff’s Office; providing an appropriation to compensate the estate for injuries sustained by M.N. and her subsequent death as a result of the negligence of the Broward County Sheriff’s Office; providing a limitation on compensation and the payment of attorney fees, etc. CLAIM: $2,500,000
FL-2027-SB34.policyArea: general relief bills and local relief bills (claims bills)
FL-2027-SB34.aiSummary: The bill would provide money to compensate the estate of M.N. for injuries and her death, which are said to have resulted from negligence by the Broward County Sheriff’s Office. It would set a limit on the compensation and on payment of attorney fees. The claim amount is $2.5 million.

FL-2027-SB20.title: Relief of Maury Hernandez by the Department of Corrections
FL-2027-SB20.summary: Relief of Maury Hernandez by the Department of Corrections; Providing for the relief of Maury Hernandez; providing an appropriation to compensate former Broward County Sheriff’s Deputy Maury Hernandez for injuries and damages sustained as a consequence of the Department of Corrections’ failures to enforce probation laws, regulations, and policies; providing legislative intent that certain liens be waived; providing a limitation on the payment of compensation and attorney fees, etc. CLAIM WITH APPROPRIATION: $5,000,000
FL-2027-SB20.policyArea: general relief bills and local relief bills (claims bills)
FL-2027-SB20.aiSummary: Would provide money to compensate former Broward County Sheriff’s Deputy Maury Hernandez for injuries and losses tied to the Department of Corrections’ failure to enforce probation rules. It also says some liens, which are legal claims on money, would be waived. The bill sets a $5,000,000 appropriation and includes limits on compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2026-HB359.summary: Search Warrants; Authorizes search warrant to be issued to recover deceased body; revises time within which certain search warrants must be returned to court; specifies time period within which search warrant issued for certain devices is considered timely executed; specifies that law enforcement agency may review data or information contained in certain devices after specified periods if devices were timely seized; provides that judge may authorize law enforcement officer applying for search warrant to appear remotely; provides that judge may authorize law enforcement officer applying for search warrant or court order to appear remotely; defines "audio-video communication technology"; authorizes law enforcement agency to obtain search warrant to use drone to conduct search in certain circumstances.

FL-2026-HB359.aiSummary: The bill changes rules for search warrants in Florida. It would let warrants be used to recover a body, set new time limits for returning warrants and for using warrants on certain devices, and allow police to review data on those devices after set periods if they were seized on time. It would also let judges allow remote appearances for warrant requests and let police seek a warrant to use a drone in some cases. It was approved by the governor and became law.

FL-2026-HB1389.aiSummary: The law changes local rules for some housing projects. Counties and cities must allow certain multifamily and mixed-use housing on some property, and they cannot use some height limits, setbacks, or stepbacks to block those projects. It also lets some applicants update their plans and allows local governments to give a density bonus, which means extra building rights, to landowners who donate land for affordable housing for military families. The law also orders a study on mezzanine finance and tiny homes for certain uses.
